entries.name: synthetic-empty
entries.notes: The degenerate case: no markers, no utility, no map bundle - so MapSpaceFactory derives no floor band, PaneSet arranges no pane, and the frame is the palette background and nothing else. That is what the committed PNG is, and it is pinned rather than skipped: 'an empty frame draws the background' is a real regression target, and a skip proves nothing. It was PENDING from the C1 merge waiting on B1/B3 to answer whether an empty level set should lay out one whole-host pane; the question is still open, and the day it is answered this golden moves and someone reviews it.

entries.name: synthetic-tenplayers
entries.notes: Ten markers over +/-2000u, both teams, one Dead and one Blinded ring, over RadarLayer's synthetic grid fallback (no map bundle). The exit-criterion render fixture, and the smallest entry that actually reaches a layer's Render - which is why BenchAllocationTests benches this one.

entries.name: synthetic-utility
entries.notes: Two smokes, six fire cells, two 40-point grenade trails, and a bomb at 0.42 detonation with a defuse in progress. The area-effect, trail and bomb-ring fixture.

entries.name: fitmap-mirage-eco
entries.notes: Markers only, both full teams, framed on the whole map over the baked de_mirage radar: the fit-map camera baseline and the simplest thing that can break the world-to-screen transform.

entries.name: duel-mirage-b
entries.notes: The layer matrix on Mirage B: four ring states with initials, a smoke, two grenade trails, a planted bomb, the baked radar, and (since D6 round 3) the two solved view cones plus the AL-to-GA could-see line. The CI budget gate benches this one, so it is also the entry that proves the vision projection allocates nothing per frame. Its kill row is IN the fixture and is NOT in the picture, deliberately: hud.killfeed is opt-in and needs a demo's kill timeline, which a headless fixture render does not have. The note claimed both were drawn, then that neither was; the vision half is now true and the kill-feed half stays false on purpose.

entries.name: bomb-planted-inferno
entries.notes: A ticking bomb mid-defuse with fire cells on the baked de_inferno radar: the bomb-ring fixture. The populated kill feed in the fixture is not drawn here - hud.killfeed is opt-in and unfeedable from a fixture; it is covered by ExportHudAndLadderTests instead.

entries.name: annotated-mirage-b
entries.notes: duel-mirage-b's frame plus burned-in ink: a static world-anchored arrow across B and a time-anchored ring around the smoke, live at tick 21120 - so the golden covers both halves of AnnotationLayer's split (the cached dry recording and the per-frame animated path). THE ONLY GOLDEN ANYWHERE THAT COVERS playback2d.annotations. The document is annotations/annotated-mirage-b.dvann.json, resolved by convention rather than by a manifest field; golden, bench and render (--ink) all read it through the production AnnotationStore. Was PENDING for B2 with no scene file at all, which is why the feature shipped uncovered.

entries.name: nuke-single-upper
entries.notes: Captured from assets/tour/sample-de_nuke.dem by 'dv2d fixture capture --tick 9694 --camera fit-alive'. Despite the name this is a STACKED render of whatever floors the frame derives - dv2d has no level-selection surface, so it cannot capture one floor. The true single-floor picture is nuke-multilevel-upper below. Renaming this entry costs a re-capture and buys nothing until the CLI grows --level.

entries.name: nuke-multilevel
entries.notes: PENDING for dv2d, permanently as things stand, and NOT because an input is missing. This golden is the PRE-V2 control's own output: captured through headless Avalonia by Playback2DGoldenCaptureTests, under the LIGHT palette the headless theme resolves, and it is gated against a delta DISTRIBUTION (99 % within +/-8, 99.5 % within +/-32, GoldenDistribution.PreV2Capture) by both of its readers - GoldenParityTests for the v2 compositor, and Playback2DGoldenCaptureTests whenever it runs off the platform that authored the corpus - because neither two rasterisers nor two OS text stacks agree pixel for pixel. dv2d renders Dark and compares at GoldenTolerance.DefaultPerceptual, which can express neither. The note here used to say 'B1 clears pending when the compositor can render it'; B1 shipped, and the reason it still cannot is the palette and the tolerance, not the pane model.

entries.name: nuke-multilevel-upper
entries.notes: PENDING for dv2d: the nuke-multilevel scene through SingleLayout with the top floor active, written and gated by LevelGoldenTests. dv2d refuses --layout single (SceneRenderPlan.RequireSingleLevelLayout) because it has no way to name a level id, so it cannot reproduce this. Listed anyway so the corpus README's 'which fixtures exist has exactly one answer' holds. This file was committed as nuke-single-upper@900x900.png - the SAME name as the 640x360 entry above, with a different meaning (D6 G-8).

entries.name: nuke-multilevel-noradar
entries.notes: PENDING for dv2d: the nuke-multilevel scene with the bundle's nav FLOORS bound but no radar images, so the canvas falls through to the grid - a map whose bundle has floors and no usable pictures is a real shape. Written and gated by LevelGoldenTests. dv2d's --no-radar disables the whole asset root, floors included, so it derives a different level set entirely; there is no flag for 'floors yes, art no'. Had NO manifest entry at all before D6.

entries.name: full-scene-budget
entries.notes: The worst-case 1080p scene design section 6's 8 ms render budget is actually stated against: 10 markers, 4 sixty-four-point trails crossing both Z bands, 12 area effects, a defusing bomb, over 2 derived levels with floor captions. Authored in code (SyntheticScenes) and committed as JSON, which BudgetFixtureCorpusTests keeps in step. Was PENDING for B1 with the scene already on disk; map/map_version claimed de_mirage while the fixture's own mapName is synthetic_budget, so a verify would have injected Mirage radar art into a synthetic scene - both are null now, which is what the fixture says.

entries.name: zones-nuke
entries.notes: The nuke-multilevel scene as a RENDERING FIXTURE ONLY for playback2d.zones: the baked de_nuke zones.json's place outlines and labels over the radar, one floor per pane, hairline in the label colour. No markers, so the picture is the outline layer plus the art under it. The scene comes from the tour sample and is evidence of nothing; ZoneResolverAgreementTests measures the resolver against real demos. A zones re-bake changes zonesVersion without touching map_version, so this golden moves without a stale-assets refusal; that is expected and is reviewed like any other visual change.

entries.name: zones-nuke-overlay
entries.notes: zones-nuke plus the user overlay zones/zones-nuke-overlay.zones.json, resolved by convention like an annotations sidecar: a custom polygon (Sandwich) drawn in the distinct dashed T-side style, a merge (BombsiteA and Hut into Site A) and a hidden place (HutRoof, re-flooded from its neighbours). The baked outline must be unchanged outside the custom polygon and the touched places. THE ONLY GOLDEN THAT COVERS AN OVERLAY.

entries.name: query-nuke-execute
entries.notes: The Query Canvas golden: de_nuke's two nav floors and radar with no markers, and six placed query tokens from queries/query-nuke-execute.dvquery.json drawn by playback2d.query. Two CT tokens on A, one CT and one T on Ramp (one per storey, which is the level-key assignment the layer has to get right), one T Outside, and one T token on the upper floor with no place, drawn hollow. The layer draws no text and the entry names no floor caption, so with zero marker labels the glyph allowance is zero and the gate is the unrelaxed one on every platform.

entries.name: result-card-nuke
entries.notes: A Result Card thumbnail (Strat Room, Result Cards And Walking): the scene SituationThumbnailRenderer.BuildFrame makes from one sampled step of a .dvrp.json.gz positions file, over de_nuke's two nav floors and radar at the card's 320x180. Eight alive markers with no label, no yaw and the team ring (a tuple carries none of those): five CT (two on A, two Outside, one on the upper Ramp) and three T (one on the lower Ramp, one in Lobby, one at Silo). Written by ResultCardThumbnailTests with RI_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1 from the same document that test renders in process, so the App's card path and dv2d's pixel gate draw one frame. Zero labels: the glyph allowance is zero and the gate is the unrelaxed one.

entries.name: overlay-nuke-execute
entries.notes: The Overlay View golden (Strat Room, Overlay View): de_nuke's two nav floors and radar with no markers, and overlays/overlay-nuke-execute.dvoverlay.json stacked over it by playback2d.overlay as a density wash per floor. A synthetic hit set of twenty-four rounds, six sampled steps each, of an A execute: CT on A, Outside and the upper Ramp with a fifth man on the lower storey, T through Lobby, Outside and the lower Ramp toward the site and one at Silo, alive counts falling with the steps. The lower-storey points must reach the lower pane only, and the CT and T clusters read in their side's colour with a blend where both stood. The layer draws no text and the entry names no floor caption, so with zero marker labels the glyph allowance is zero and the gate is the unrelaxed one on every platform.
